thread:
Noah Rivera: Quick help please  my partner gave birth yesterday, baby in NICU. Hospital says they'll hold billing but wants preauth for some neonatal consults. We thought those were covered but I can't find the preauth paperwork. Coverage effective 2025-06-01. Any quick steps?

Maya - People Ops: Congrats and sorry you're dealing with this stress. Neonatal inpatient consults are usually covered as emergent inpatient services. Preauth isn't always required for emergency admissions, but some specialty consults (e.g., surgical consults, neonatology subspecialty procedures) can need prior auth for non-emergent add-ons. First: upload the hospital's request for preauth or the consult order to Benefits Portal > Claims Help > Urgent NICU. We'll open with carrier right away.

Noah Rivera: Uploading the consult order now (redacted names). Hospital billing said "please provide member policy confirmation and prior auth for postnatal consults". They also asked for baby member ID  we don't have a member ID yet for the newborn.

Benefits Bot: Reminder: newborns are typically covered retroactively if added within 30 days of birth. For immediate needs, carriers accept a hospital letter of birth + parent's member ID to process inpatient claims. Upload the birth certificate/stamped hospital letter and request temporary newborn coverage ID via People Ops.

Maya - People Ops: We'll request a Temporary Neonate Coverage Letter and a provisional member ID for the baby. @Claims Team can you trigger a carrier emergent review using parent's member ID and the hospital letter? We'll note this as "Urgent - NICU admission".

Claims Team: On it. We need: parent's member ID (last 4 via DM), infant DOB, hospital account number, and the consult order. We'll submit an urgent case to ZenithCare with a request to waive preauth due to emergent admission. ETA initial response 24-48 hours. If carrier requires retro enrollment for the baby, we can add the infant retro to the policy and process claims.

Noah Rivera: DM'd last 4 and hospital acct #. Also uploaded the hospital letter of birth and order. Appreciate the quick triage.

NICU Liaison: FYI hospitals sometimes use the newborn as "dependent pending" and will accept an authorization using parent's member info. We can also get a caseworker to call the hospital billing office and provide the carrier case number. That usually prevents collections and gets the consult started.

Maya - People Ops: Also flagging Finance Ops in case any deposits or interim payments are requested by the hospital. @Finance Ops if hospital insists on a deposit we may need to arrange an interim hardship pay so family isn't out of pocket.

Finance Ops: Noted. If deposit is requested and family is unable to pay, we can issue an interim hardship payment up to $5k pending carrier adjudication. We'll need a copy of the hospital invoice and a short attestation from People Ops. Noah, DM receipt if they request payment.

Claims Team: Update: Carrier case submitted (ZC-NICU-5599). We flagged as emergency and requested preauth waiver for consults during admission. Will update in this thread once carrier confirms or requests more docs.

Noah Rivera: Thank you all so much  hospital said they received the carrier case number and will hold billing. This helps a ton. I'll upload any receipts if something changes.

Maya - People Ops: Keeping thread open. If carrier approves, we'll also add the baby to the policy retroactively. If denied, we'll escalate with clinical notes and ask for peer-to-peer review. Please avoid posting any full member IDs or SSNs here. DM or portal only. Sending best wishes to your family.
